newsitem.title: UK: Angerstein H1 earnings rise 17.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Angerstein H1 earnings rise 17.5 pct.

text.p: Angerstein Underwriting, one of the largest corporate investors at Lloyd's of London, on Wednesday reported double digit increases in revenues and earnings for the six months to November 30.

The investment trust, which last week completed the acquisition of member's agency Stace Barr Wellington, said net revenue after tax had risen 17.5 percent to 1.94 million stg and earnings per share 17.9 percent to 1.64 pence.
The interim dividend was up 9.1 percent to 1.2 pence.
The increase in earnings reflects continued strong growth in dividend income from equities together with the emergence of cost savings from last year's acquisition of Lloyd's investment trust Delian.
The group's net asset value per share at November 30 was 107.6 pence, an increase of 6.1 percent over the period.
Angerstein said it was forecasting returns of at least 7.5 percent of capacity for the 1994 underwriting year and 7.1 percent for 1995.

While it was too early to form any definite views about 1996 underwriting, it said it drew some comfort from the relative infrequency of insured catastrophe losses in the calendar year, especially against a background of weaker market conditions.
